nit: I would prefer setting the gpio values (`muxToBMC`, `muxToDevice`) to be written down in this function.

I feel like that's more in line with C++ semantics since we acquire the gpios (as a resource) but i don't consider gpio control itself to be a resource, conceptually.

From my perspective:
- `lineBulk->request(config, groupValues[chipName]);` -> resource
- `muxToDevice` / `muxToBMC` -> control action, not a resource

It's a matter of perspective i guess but i feel like the code would be more straightforward that way. What do you think?

Yes, I agree with your opinion. I simplified the code, but also added a comment in gpio_controller.hpp to clarify when the mux status is switched.
This should make the control flow easier to follow while keeping the code concise.
Would you prefer that I keep it this way, or move the GPIO control (muxToBMC / muxToDevice) into this function as you suggested?

i guess both approaches have their advantages.

Your solution prevents accidentally leaving the gpios in the wrong state as they are switched back on destruction.

Yes, removing std::move() would still compile and work.
However, std::move() avoids copying — it allows the member variables (lines_ and polarities_) to be move-constructed instead of copy-constructed.
Since lines_ and polarities_ are not static vectors and may have multiple instances, using std::move() helps improve performance and efficiency by preventing unnecessary memory copies.

You have added MuxOutput as an optional property https://grok.openbmc.org/xref/openbmc/entity-manager/schemas/cpld.json?r=46906e5d3e9df92cf5ac495d21dc041f51f52fe9 Please handle it accordingly.

For this part, I’m not sure I fully understand.
In entity-manager, MuxOutputs is not a required field, but here I don’t see any function or option that allows us to treat it as an optional input.
@Henry_WU@quantatw.com, If MuxOutputs is expected to be a required field, then lets make this a required field in EM schema as well.

However, not all CPLDs need to trigger the mux, so this should not be a required property.
Currently, we are using dbusGetRequiredProperty because it is the only function available in dbus_helper.hpp.
Maybe the function name should have the word “Required” removed, since it is not always appropriate for optional properties?

@Henry_WU@quantatw.com This is the with the long term intent that Dbus properties have fixed fields. Currently muxOutputs is an array. For any CPLD which doesn't need to trigger the mux can send this list as empty from EM side and this code shall handle it accordingly. So, lets mark this property as required in EM schema.

@paligill@gmail.com nit: Making the MuxOutputs property required in EM means all existing platform EM configurations that already define the CPLDFirmware field must be updated to explicitly add an empty []. This change introduces a mandatory but functionally redundant field for platforms that don't use mux outputs. Is this requirement intentional, or should MuxOutputs remain optional to avoid unnecessary config change across platforms?

@kevin.tung.openbmc@gmail.com Ideally i would prefer to keep the schema fixed so Dbus properties are fixed as well. But since here we are not using PDI bindings for now we can keep this code as such. Just make sure the optional properties are handled appropriately. If this is true, please resolve this comment.

1. No, it still works without std::move() — the move constructor/assignment is used mainly as defensive programming.

2. No, releaseAll() simply releases ownership of the GPIO lines back to the kernel.

should this be muxToHost instead?

Not all muxes switch between the BMC and the host.
For example, the debug-card-mux is used to cut off the connection between the CPLD and the debug card, rather than switching ownership between the BMC and host.

Because of this, I named the function muxToDevice() instead of assuming all muxes are BMC–host switches.
